farmer_reported_issue: Sudden wilting of scattered cotton plants after heavy rain followed by bright sunshine. Soil is black clayey loam.
diagnosis: Para-wilt (Physiological Wilt) caused by sudden root asphyxiation / oxygen depletion in saturated soil followed by high transpiration demand.
verified_prescription: Do NOT apply chemical fungicides. Drench plant basin with 1% Copper Oxychloride (30g in 10L water) only if collar rot is observed. For para-wilt: Spray 1% Urea (10g/L) + 1% Potassium Nitrate (KNO3 @ 10g/L) or 2% DAP solution to revive root absorption. Lightly stir soil around plants with hoe to allow root aeration.
outcome: 90% of wilted plants revived within 72 hours; normal boll formation resumed.

farmer_reported_issue: Greyish water-soaked oval lesions on lower leaf sheaths near water line with brown undulating margins. Farmer intended to mix Monocrotophos with Carbendazim.
diagnosis: Sheath Blight caused by Rhizoctonia solani. Stopped farmer from using Monocrotophos (ineffective against fungal sheath blight and hazardous).
verified_prescription: Drain excess water from field to keep water level below 2 cm. Apply Hexaconazole 5% SC @ 400 ml/acre or Validamycin 3% L @ 400 ml/acre in 200L water directed at the stem base. Repeat after 12 days if disease progresses.
outcome: Disease contained at lower leaf sheaths; no neck infection occurred.

farmer_reported_issue: Downward leaf curling with elongated petiole ('inverted cup' symptom), plants looking dark green and brittle.
diagnosis: Yellow Mite (Polyphagotarsonemus latus) infestation. Distinct from thrips which cause upward curling.
verified_prescription: Apply Spiromesifen 22.9% SC @ 200 ml/acre or Propergite 57% EC @ 400 ml/acre in 200L water. Ensure fine mist spray covering underside of leaves where mites colonize.
outcome: Fresh foliage emerged normal within 10 days; flower drop halted.
